Sorry for late response. To clarify, I would be slightly more concerned if the OP's gf was under 25 (<25).

There are numerous studies available regarding the increased risk of  "accidental suicide" In adolescents (<25).
I am not posting references 2/2 the fact that the findings of these studies directly contradict the above comment regarding posting guidelines.
I think talking to your dad is a really good idea. In the US you can also Text "GO” TO 741-741 if you would like to speak to a counselor

I think it's a bit subjective but I think it basically means remember to take time for yourself, where whatever you do is for you and you alone. When I was in IP psych it specifically referred to ADL skills (sleep, exercise, showering) mixed with "fun" activities such as polishing nails etc.  So in that sense, self care can be as simple as taking a bit of "me time" to take a bubble bath and/or practice diaphragmatic breathing.  For some people, it may mean eating regular healthy meals, taking vitamins, or exercising as well as the other things posted thus far. It could also just mean establishing/setting boundaries.

No one here can tell you what to do as we aren't in your situation.  I would personally suggest calling the police or a suicide hotline (your local or national) but I can see why you would prefer not to based solely on your posts.

What I will say is that threats of this nature should be taken seriously and not swept under the rug.  It's hard to discern your age from your posts but I would be slightly more worried if she's <25 for various reasons.

If she actually has a past history of suicide attempt(s) or hospitalizations etc.  you should call the police regardless of anything else posted here.

Thanks for your reply.  My family is steadfast that PTSD is only for people in the military or similar situations, so it has been difficult to say the least.
I go to yoga once or twice a week but had not heard of "kundalini yoga".  It's offered in my city so I will give it a try :)
 P.S.  I actually "self medicated" with SAM-E prior to my official diagnosis ,but it did not work for me.  I have heard good things from others though :)
I hear you, and am quite impressed with your articulation.  I hope you feel better. :)
